test.name: Both summaries survive a delegation that does not name them
test.description: The dual-output invariant under a delegation the agent does not author. ut_project_status_008 grades the same contract, but its delegation spells the contract out ('the user-friendly summary first, then the detailed GPS-state summary'), so a pass there cannot distinguish an agent that holds the contract from one that is reading it off the prompt. This delegation is the wording a live Cowork orchestrator actually produced (measured 2026-10-02): a bare restatement of the user's ask, naming neither summary. The direct arm has no router between the agent and the grader, so a miss here is the agent's, not the relay's.

judge_context: The run must produce BOTH summaries in a single response: (1) a plain-language user-friendly narrative AND (2) a detailed GPS-state summary. Producing only one of the two is a fail of the dual-output invariant

The delegation deliberately does not ask for either summary by name. That is the point of this test: the agent's own body requires both, so both are required here. Do not treat the terse delegation as licence to produce a single summary, and do not penalize the agent for producing more than the delegation literally asked for

The detailed summary should show GPS-structured state: question status, GPS-element progress, plan/log statistics, evidence counts, conflicts, hypotheses, exhaustiveness level, conclusion readiness, and proof tier

The user-friendly summary should tell the story in plain language and AVOID GPS jargon (e.g. not 'primary source', 'indirect evidence', 'information quality') — explaining reliability conversationally instead
Both summaries should be internally consistent with each other and with research.json (same counts, same recommended next step)
